He had learned to admit he was licked, take stock of himself and confess his defects to another person, make restitution, give of himself, and pray to whatever God he thought there was, even as an experiment (A.A. A GSR attends district meetings and area assemblies with a vote, reports back to the group, and passes on the group's views. The manual suggests at least two years' sobriety. P-16, <1>The A.A. Group</1> (© 2018), calls the GSR "the group’s link with the General Service Conference" (P-16).
6c7216172da8: <0>District.</0> A cluster of groups near one another (the manual also describes language districts and, since the pandemic, virtual districts for online groups). The GSRs elect a <1>DCM</1>, who sits on the area committee. On how a DCM should lead, the manual says the GSRs will want "to be inspired and encouraged, but not told what to do" (The A.A. Service Manual, 2024–2026, Chapter 2).
385cce96f8c2: <0>Area.</0> "The U.S. and Canada are divided into 93 geographic areas" (The A.A. Service Manual, 2024–2026, Glossary), usually one per state or province, more where A.A. is large. The area assembly is made up of GSRs, DCMs, area officers and committee chairs. Every two years an election assembly chooses the delegate, usually by the Third Legacy Procedure: a two-thirds vote, or names drawn from a hat. The area also runs services too big for one group, such as public information, corrections and treatment facility work.
baba535454bf: <0>Delegate and Conference.</0> The delegate serves two years and goes to the Conference each spring in New York. It has about 135 voting members; area delegates "make up at least two-thirds of the Conference body" (The A.A. Service Manual, 2024–2026, Introduction), with the trustees, the directors of A.A. World Services and the Grapevine, and staff. Matters approved by two-thirds become Advisory Actions, and the delegate reports back to the area and its GSRs.
714073df5190: <0>Not bosses.</0> The current manual quotes Bill in "the first edition of this manual" (our copy gives no date; the manual grew out of his Third Legacy Manual, first drafted in 1951): "The Conference represents us, but cannot rule us" (The A.A. Service Manual, 2024–2026, Chapter 6). Concept XII (1962) bars the Conference from "any acts of government" (Twelve Concepts for World Service, Concept XII).
4c2391748742: <0>Not the intergroup.</0> Intergroups and central offices keep local meeting lists and phones. The manual says they are an important part of A.A. but "they are not part of the general service structure or a satellite of GSO" (The A.A. Service Manual, 2024–2026, Introduction).

c33a2a1fa4db: Henrietta Seiberling was a nonalcoholic member of the Oxford Group in Akron, the daughter-in-law of the founder of the Goodyear rubber company. She lived in the gatehouse of the Seiberling estate.
4527bf91c6bb: On the Saturday before Mother's Day, May 1935, Bill W., stranded in Akron and afraid he would drink, reached her by telephone after a minister's list of names ran out. She knew of a doctor in her Oxford Group who couldn't stop drinking, and the next afternoon she brought Dr. Bob and Bill together in her home.
7f088260da42: Bill wrote that she was the only one on that list "who had understood enough and cared enough" (A.A. Comes of Age, 1957), and that A.A.'s debt to her was beyond reckoning. Dr. Bob called her "our good friend Henrietta."
932e975020a2: In his last major talk, printed in P-53, Dr. Bob named her. At the end of Bill's list, "his eyes happened to light on the name of Mrs. Seiberling — our good friend Henrietta" (P-53). She told him, "Come right out and have lunch with me." (P-53), and after hearing his story, "I have just the man for you." (P-53). When Anne put her off, "But Henry is very persistent, a very determined individual." (P-53), and the visit was set for the next day, Sunday and Mother's Day (P-53).
8c7888beb2c4: He also recalled asking her, while still drinking, whether she thought he really wanted to stop. She said: "No, Bob, I think you want to. You just haven't found a way to work it yet." (P-53).
f853cd5222c9: Bill says hers was the last name on a list of about ten from the Rev. Walter Tunks (A.A. Comes of Age, 1957). He remembered an elderly Mr. Seiberling, Goodyear's founder, and hesitated to call his wife; when he did, a young Southern voice answered, a Seiberling daughter-in-law (A.A. Comes of Age, 1957). She said: "I'm no alcoholic, but I've had my difficulties." (A.A. Comes of Age, 1957), and invited him out: "I live in the gatehouse of the Seiberling place." (A.A. Comes of Age, 1957). She had found her answers in the Oxford Groups (A.A. Comes of Age, 1957). The next afternoon Dr. Bob and Anne came to her door, and she put the two men in her library (A.A. Comes of Age, 1957).
c7edbf471d51: Bill set his thanks on record: of the ten people on the list, "Henrietta was the only one who had understood enough and cared enough." (A.A. Comes of Age, 1957). That first summer she counseled alcoholics' families as Anne did (A.A. Comes of Age, 1957). "What Alcoholics Anonymous owes to her will always be beyond anybody's reckoning." (A.A. Comes of Age, 1957). Bill adds that she and the Williamses had tried hard to help Dr. Bob before he came, sharing their own defects with him (A.A. Comes of Age, 1957).

It says she was a Vassar graduate with three teenage children, all in the Oxford Group (Dr. Bob and the Good Oldtimers, 1980). In March or April 1935, before Bill came, a friend asked her what could be done about Bob Smith; she arranged an Oxford Group meeting at the Williamses' at which members shared costly things, and Dr. Bob told them: "I am a secret drinker" (Dr. Bob and the Good Oldtimers, 1980). Praying for him the next morning, she received what she called guidance: "Bob must not touch one drop of alcohol." (Dr. Bob and the Good Oldtimers, 1980).
71baf5b227c5: She remembered Bill's call on May 11, 1935 this way: "I'm from the Oxford Group, and I'm a rum hound from New York." (Dr. Bob and the Good Oldtimers, 1980), and her thought: "This is really manna from heaven." (Dr. Bob and the Good Oldtimers, 1980). She arranged for Bill to stay at a nearby country club so he could remain in Akron (Dr. Bob and the Good Oldtimers, 1980).
83db576060df: The same book shows her differences with the alcoholics later on. She thought A.A. should not raise money and that it wasn't putting enough emphasis on God; she told Bill, "We are out to please God." (Dr. Bob and the Good Oldtimers, 1980).
